name: Vint
description: Vint ('Screw') is a Russian partnership trick-taking game that influenced Contract Bridge's development. 4 players in 2 teams. 52-card deck. 13 each. Bidding (1-7 tricks over 6) with suit/NT denominations. NO dummy — all play own hands. Both sides score below-the-line for tricks won. First to 500 wins.

content.text: Vint ('Screw') is a Russian partnership trick-taking game that influenced Contract Bridge's development. 4 players in 2 teams. 52-card deck. 13 each. Bidding (1-7 tricks over 6) with suit/NT denominations. NO dummy — all play own hands. Both sides score below-the-line for tricks won. First to 500 wins.

Vint emerged in Russia in the latter half of the 19th century; primitive forms were known as Siberian vint. It was fashionable in late 19th-century Russia and featured bidding and scoring that foreshadowed Contract Bridge. The Russian word Vint (винт) means 'screw', referring to the rotating auction. It declined after the revolution but survived in Finland as Skruuvi and reached North America, influencing Contract Bridge in the 1920s.
The cards are shuffled and cut; 13 cards are dealt to each player, one at a time face down, clockwise.
